extracted.intended_audience: startup founders, PR professionals, and communications teams pitching TechCrunch reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing and sending newsworthy press pitches to TechCrunch reporters, covering what topics they cover, formatting requirements, embargo/exclusivity rules, and signals that speed or slow coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startups raising funding (Seed through Series C+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Startups raising funding (Seed through Series C+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TechCrunch covers funding announcements for startups in these stages; include investor references for funding announcements (see 'What Speeds Up Coverage').

rubrics_metrics.name: Product launches with new technical capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Product launches with new technical capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on genuine technical novelty or capabilities rather than marketing fluff; include multimedia and concrete metrics where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder stories with substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder stories with substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch narratives that offer real insights, evidence, or notable context about the founder or team rather than lightweight profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry analysis and trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry analysis and trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data, concrete metrics, or expert viewpoints that justify a trend story; context matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition and exit news
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition and exit news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key deal terms, credible spokespeople, and context about the strategic significance of the exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis and controversy in tech
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis and controversy in tech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide evidence, documentation, and spokespeople; timely, verifiable details speed coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stealth-stage companies with no product — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Stealth-stage companies with no product are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching companies that lack a demonstrable product or customer evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 'we use AI' claims — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic 'we use AI' claims are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about AI must be specific and substantive; vague AI marketing language will be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: B2B SaaS announcements without major customers — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: B2B SaaS announcements without major customers are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include customer references, logos, or notable deployments to make B2B SaaS newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine partnerships or integrations — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine partnerships or integrations are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships must have notable strategic significance or big-name participants to be considered newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire announcements unless executive is well-known — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire announcements are only considered if the executive is well-known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive hires should have strong news value (e.g., established public figures) to warrant coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity awards — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Vanity awards are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching awards or lists that lack independent significance or verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most enterprise software news — not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Most enterprise software news is not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enterprise software needs major customers, measurable outcomes, or exceptional angles to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email to relevant reporter (not info@)
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the pitch as an email to the relevant reporter — do not use generic inboxes like info@.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and email the reporter who covers the relevant beat or topic; personalize to their recent coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: news in 8 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line should present the news in 8 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the subject concise and news-first (the Quality Rubric repeats: 'Subject line news-first').

rubrics_metrics.name: Body length: 100-200 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch body should be 100-200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and focused; include the most newsworthy facts up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized to recent coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize the pitch to the reporter's recent coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference a recent article or explain why the story fits the reporter's beat to increase relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include spokesperson availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Include spokesperson availability in the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State when founders/spokespeople can speak and be available, ideally within 24 hours for speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a phone number
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a phone number in the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct phone number makes it easy for reporters to follow up quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo acceptance from trusted PR contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: TechCrunch accepts embargoes from trusted PR contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes are allowed when submitted by trusted PR; establish trust through prior relationships or credible agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard embargo window: 24-48 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: 24-48 hours is the standard embargo window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short embargo windows are typical; clarify the embargo time and ensure spokespeople can meet it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo break consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embargo is broken, TechCrunch will not provide future coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect embargo terms — breaking them harms future media relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusives: only one reporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusives are offered only to one reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TechCrunch does not accept co-exclusives; an exclusive should be truly exclusive to one reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: No co-exclusives
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-exclusives are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not offer the same exclusive to multiple outlets if claiming exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-attached multimedia speeds coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-attached multimedia (screenshots, video) speeds coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach high-quality, ready-to-use images and video so reporters can immediately evaluate and use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer references with logos and quotes speed coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer references with logos and quotes speed coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable customer references and permission to use logos/quotes to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor references for funding announcements speed coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Investor references help speed coverage for funding announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List participating investors and context; notable investors increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder availability within 24 hours speeds coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder being available within 24 hours speeds coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast availability for interviews increases the chance of timely coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete metrics provided speed coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing concrete metrics (revenue, users, growth rate) speeds coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verifiable, specific metrics rather than vague claims; include supporting evidence if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story angle that fits TechCrunch voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A story angle that fits TechCrunch's voice speeds coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the narrative to TechCrunch's editorial perspective and the reporter's beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertain spokesperson availability slows coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: If spokesperson availability is uncertain, coverage is slowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state availability windows and ensure spokespeople can commit to interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia behind a request form slows coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia that requires a request form to access slows coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct attachments or accessible links rather than gated assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vague metrics or unverifiable claims slow coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague metrics or unverifiable claims slow or prevent coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to substantiate numbers and avoid unverified assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press kit with PDFs only slows coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Press kits composed only of PDFs slow coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multimedia in web-accessible formats and attach assets rather than only PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient context for the news slows coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient context about why the news matters slows coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain impact, relevance, and provide comparisons or benchmarks as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching during major news cycles slows coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching during major news cycles slows or buries coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching at times when bigger stories dominate the news agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story doesn't fit our beat — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If the story doesn't fit TechCrunch's beat, it often receives no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target pitches to reporters and beats that match the story topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Already covered similar story recently — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If TechCrunch has covered a similar story recently, you may get no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check recent coverage and explain what is genuinely new or different.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers don't justify coverage — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If the numbers (metrics, scale) don't justify coverage, there may be no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide convincing metrics or evidence of impact to justify newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson not credible — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: A spokesperson perceived as not credible can lead to no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use credible spokespeople and be prepared to back claims with evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitched too many reporters at once — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitched too many reporters at once can result in no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mass-blasting reporters; personalize and target your outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not enough novelty in the news — common no-response reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of novelty in the news can lead to no response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize what is new, surprising, or impactful about the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: story fits our specific beats
rubrics_metrics.description: Story must fit TechCrunch's specific beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the pitch matches the publication's topical focus (see 'What We Cover').

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: subject line news-first
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line should be news-first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the news in the subject line rather than promotional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: personalized to reporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch must be personalized to the reporter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference recent reporting or explain the fit to the reporter's beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: multimedia pre-attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia should be pre-attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready-to-use images, screenshots, or video with the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: concrete metrics provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete metrics as part of the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify scale, growth, revenue, or user numbers with verifiable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: spokesperson available
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson(s) must be available for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List availability windows and provide direct contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric: embargo respected if offered
rubrics_metrics.description: If an embargo is offered, it must be respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor embargo terms to maintain future trust and coverage opportunities.
